report.incident_title: Checkout fully down right after this morning's checkout deploy
report.summary: Checkout is failing because the mTLS certificate used by payments-svc (Certificate/payments-svc-mtls, issued by internal-ca) expired at 09:14:00Z on 2026-08-03. Checkout's payment authorize calls fail the TLS handshake with "x509: certificate has expired", and the 5xx rate went from ~0.3% to ~94-95%. The certificate was not renewed because a platform RBAC change on 2026-07-28 (PR #2231) removed cert-manager's get/list on issuers in the payments namespace. Renewal began failing on 07-31 at 09:14, exactly 72h before expiry, and kept failing with a 24h backoff. No alert fired for certificate expiry or for the IssuingFailed events. The checkout v3.8.1 deploy is not the cause: it changed only an email template, and v3.8.0 pods fail identically. The on-call rollback did take effect, but it cannot fix an expired certificate, so errors continue on both versions. The fix is to restore a valid payments-svc-mtls certificate and correct the RBAC, not to roll checkout back or forward.
report.root_cause: payments-svc-mtls certificate (internal-ca) expired at 2026-08-03T09:14:00Z. Automatic renewal had been failing since 2026-07-31 09:14Z because cert-manager lost RBAC to read issuers in the payments namespace after the least-privilege ClusterRole change (PR #2231, 2026-07-28). Nothing alerted on the failed renewals or the expiry.

hypotheses.statement: payments-svc-mtls certificate expired because cert-manager renewal was blocked by the RBAC tightening (PR #2231), so checkout's mTLS handshakes to payments-svc fail.

facts.text: checkout-svc errors start at 09:14:02Z: 'authentication handshake failed: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid: current time ... is after 2026-08-03T09:14:00Z'. Both v3.8.0 and v3.8.1 pods show the error.

payments-svc logs a TLS WARN at 09:14:06Z ('client offered only unsupported/expired chain; handshake aborted (peer=checkout-svc)') and inbound_tls_handshake_failures jumps from 0 to ~1830-1912/min at 09:15, with 0 before.

cert-manager IssuingFailed on 07-31 09:14Z and 08-02 09:14Z: 'issuers.cert-manager.io "internal-ca" is forbidden: ... cannot get resource "issuers" in namespace "payments"'. Retry backoff 24h; renewBefore=72h.
Platform change on 2026-07-28 15:02Z: 'Tighten cert-manager ClusterRole to least privilege (PR #2231). Removed get/list on issuers.cert-manager.io for namespaces outside cert-manager.'
No alerts for payments-svc from 07-25 onward, so no expiry or IssuingFailed alert fired.

assumptions: The expired certificate is the payments-svc server certificate, as the topology note says payments-svc requires mTLS and its server cert comes from cert-manager. The WARN line in payments-svc refers to a client chain, so the exact side is inferred and not directly confirmed.

hypotheses.statement: The checkout-svc v3.8.1 deploy (09:08) caused the outage and the rollback should have fixed it.

facts.text: The v3.8.1 change touched only templates/email/order_confirmation.html (email copy). It does not touch the payment path.
Errors are on v3.8.0 pods too (09:14:02Z pod checkout-svc-41c-d, and 09:24:15Z pod checkout-svc-41c-q, which runs v3.8.0 after rollback). The failure is version-independent.
After the 09:22 rollback to v3.8.0, the v3.8.0 5xx rate stayed at 94.6-95.3% from 09:20 to 09:45.

hypotheses.statement: The rollback did not take effect (the reporter's suspicion).

facts.text: Post-rollback logs still show v3.8.0 pods failing, so the rollback is not visible as a fix.
Pod logs at 09:24Z show version v3.8.0 running, which matches the rollback record at 09:22Z. The rollback was applied, but the errors came from the certificate, so it could not fix the outage.

hypotheses.statement: An external or downstream outage in payments-svc or psp-gateway caused the failures, not a certificate problem.

facts.text: payments-svc logs show only TLS handshake failures, with no application errors or PSP errors in the window.
The checkout errors are explicit x509 expiry messages, matching the cert-manager expiry at the same second.

assumptions: psp-gateway health was not queried directly. The evidence points to the TLS layer before any PSP call.

corrective_actions.action: Restore a valid payments-svc-mtls certificate now. Either manually re-issue it from internal-ca into the payments namespace secret (a platform-admin action), or temporarily grant cert-manager get/list on issuers in the payments namespace so it can renew. Then restart or reload checkout-svc and payments-svc so they pick up the new chain. Confirm checkout 5xx returns to ~0.3% and inbound_tls_handshake_failures returns to 0.
corrective_actions.rationale: The outage is an expired certificate. Only a valid certificate on the payments-svc side stops the handshake failures. Rolling checkout back or forward cannot fix it, as shown by the v3.8.0 pods still failing after the rollback.

corrective_actions.action: Fix PR #2231 so cert-manager can read issuers in every namespace that holds a Certificate (for example a RoleBinding in payments scoped to issuers get/list). Confirm the renewal succeeds with a dry run or by forcing a renewal, and check that IssuingFailed events clear.
corrective_actions.rationale: The RBAC tightening removed the permission cert-manager needs to renew. Without this fix the certificate will expire again when the replacement expires.

corrective_actions.action: Add alerts for cert-manager IssuingFailed events and for certificate notAfter within 14, 7 and 1 days. Alert on inbound_tls_handshake_failures spikes, which would have caught this at 09:15 (the first failures) and earlier at the renewal failures on 07-31.
corrective_actions.rationale: No alert fired during the 72h window in which renewal was failing, or at expiry. The IssuingFailed events and the handshake-failure metric were already available, so these alerts would have fired early.

corrective_actions.action: Require a renewal smoke test (or a cert-manager dry-run as part of the CI or policy check) for any RBAC change to cert-manager. Document a runbook for expired internal certificates; none exists today (search returned no runbook).
corrective_actions.rationale: The RBAC change passed review without testing renewal. A pre-merge renewal check would have caught the lost permission. The absence of a runbook slowed recovery.

corrective_actions.action: Do not roll checkout forward or back to fix this incident. The v3.8.1 email-copy change is not the cause, so it can be re-deployed once the certificate is fixed. Keep checkout on v3.8.0 until the certificate is confirmed healthy to reduce change risk during recovery.
corrective_actions.rationale: Holding checkout on v3.8.0 avoids mixing a second change into the recovery. The email change is unrelated to the failure and can ship later on its own.

missing_data: Whether checkout-svc needs a restart to reload the new certificate chain is unknown. Check how checkout caches the payments-svc trust bundle.
The exact contents of PR #2231 (only the summary was returned), and whether other namespaces' certificates are also affected by the RBAC change.
No direct health check on psp-gateway (external). The logs suggest the failure is at the TLS layer, before the PSP call.
No certificate expiry alert or inventory of other certificates with a notAfter in the next few days, so other expiries are unchecked.

The payments-svc WARN says 'client offered only unsupported/expired chain'. This is ambiguous about which side's certificate expired. The cert-manager event for payments-svc-mtls and the checkout x509 error both point to the server certificate, but the owner of the trust path should confirm.
questions_for_human: Who can re-issue payments-svc-mtls right now, and is an RBAC grant on issuers acceptable under the least-privilege policy from PR #2231?
Does checkout-svc or payments-svc need a restart to load the renewed certificate? Is there a rolling-restart runbook for this?
Which other certificates managed by cert-manager are affected by the same RBAC change, and when do they expire?
Should the checkout v3.8.1 email change be re-deployed once the certificate is fixed, or held?
